preconditions.description: Initial heads h, tails t, and limit R are non-negative integers not exceeding 200.
The initial total number of heads and tails is positive and does not exceed R.
The maximum number of heads (n) and tails (m) that can be cut in one strike are between 1 and 200.
The input provides exactly n pairs for head growth rules and m pairs for tail growth rules.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= dh and 0 <= dt for (dh, dt) in head_growth_rules + tail_growth_rules)
preconditions.description: All growth values (heads and tails) specified in the rules are non-negative.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is one of the three valid outcome strings.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'Ivan' implies (int(output_lines[1]) == min_blows_to_win and min_blows_to_win is finite)
postconditions.description: If Ivan wins, the second line is the minimum number of blows required to reach (0, 0) from the initial state without the total ever exceeding R.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'Draw' implies (min_blows_to_win is infinite and max_survival_blows is infinite)
postconditions.description: If the outcome is a Draw, it is impossible to win, but there exists a strategy to survive indefinitely without the total exceeding R.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'Zmey' implies (min_blows_to_win is infinite and max_survival_blows is finite and int(output_lines[1]) == max_survival_blows)
postconditions.description: If Zmey wins, it is impossible to win or draw, and the second line is the maximum number of blows Ivan can make before the total exceeds R, assuming optimal play to delay defeat.
The output consists of exactly two lines.
